wizard.title: Set up AgentCRM
wizard.subtitle: Your CRM, your storage. Nothing runs on our servers — there are none.

terms.title: Before you start
terms.hint: AgentCRM is a static app: it runs in your browser (or in the agentcrm CLI) and talks directly to storage you own.

points.static: No AgentCRM server: the admin is static files, your data goes straight from this browser to your storage.
points.yourData: You choose where the data lives (your bucket, your repository, your Firebase project, this browser) and you can move it later.
points.secrets: Keys, tokens and passphrases stay in each browser (or the CLI credentials file). They are never written to config.js nor to the data.
points.gdpr: You are the controller of the personal data you store. Files are encrypted by default, and deleted records can be purged physically.
points.warranty: The software is provided as is, without warranty. Keep backups (Settings → Data backend → Export).

terms.accept: I understand and want to continue
terms.quickHint: Use This browser: no account, no storage to configure, demo data included.

data.title: Where should your CRM data live?
data.hint: You can transfer everything to another backend later (Settings → Data backend), ids preserved.

journal.title: Encrypted file on my storage
journal.description: An S3 / R2 / OVH bucket, a private git repo or a local folder. End-to-end encrypted with your passphrase.
journal.details: Each change is appended as an encrypted file; teammates who have the storage keys and the passphrase see each other's edits within seconds. No account system: whoever has the keys + passphrase is admin.

firebase.title: Firebase
firebase.description: Firestore + Firebase Auth in your own Google project. Real-time, accounts with admin / member / viewer roles.
firebase.details: Best for teams: everyone signs in with email/password or Google, roles are enforced by Firestore security rules generated for you. Free tier is plenty for a small team.

git-json.title: Private git repository
git-json.description: One JSON file per record in a private GitHub / GitLab repo (or a local clone). One commit per change.
git-json.details: Each user signs in with their own token; their repository permission becomes their role. Full history and diffs — but the history keeps every past version of personal data.

local.title: This browser
local.description: Data stays in this browser (IndexedDB). Single user, no account — ideal to try AgentCRM.
local.details: Nothing leaves this browser. Clearing the site data deletes the CRM: export or transfer it to a real backend before relying on it.

location.journalHint: Use a PRIVATE location dedicated to this CRM. The browser talks to it directly (CORS must allow the admin's origin — see docs/hosting.md).

s3.title: S3-compatible bucket
s3.description: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, OVHcloud, Scaleway, MinIO…

github.title: GitHub repository
github.description: A private repo; encrypted files are committed with your token.

gitlab.title: GitLab repository
gitlab.description: A private project on gitlab.com or self-managed.

local-folder.title: Local folder
local-folder.description: A folder on this computer (Chrome / Edge), e.g. synced by Dropbox or a NAS.

s3PresetHints.aws: Create a private bucket and an IAM user limited to it (s3:GetObject, PutObject, DeleteObject, ListBucket).
s3PresetHints.r2: Endpoint: https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com — create an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on this bucket only. Region: auto.
s3PresetHints.ovh: Endpoint: https://s3.<region>.io.cloud.ovh.net (e.g. gra, sbg, de). Create S3 credentials for a user limited to this container.
s3PresetHints.scaleway: Endpoint: https://s3.<region>.scw.cloud (fr-par, nl-ams, pl-waw). Use an API key scoped to Object Storage.
s3PresetHints.minio: Self-hosted MinIO: use an access key limited to this bucket. Path-style addressing is required.
s3PresetHints.other: Any S3-compatible service with SigV4 signing and CORS support.

location.localFolderHint: The browser keeps access to this folder; after a reload you'll be asked to re-grant it with one click.
location.folderUnsupported: This browser can't open local folders (File System Access API). Use Chrome or Edge, or choose another storage.
location.rootHelp: The CRM files go under this path (e.g. agentcrm). Use another path to keep several CRMs on the same storage.
location.fillRequired: Fill in the required fields first.
location.publicRepoEncrypted: Warning: this repository is PUBLIC. Your files are encrypted, but make the repository private anyway.
location.existingTitle: An AgentCRM workspace already exists here
location.existingEncrypted: It is encrypted. Join it with its passphrase, or use another folder to create a new CRM.
location.existingPlain: It is not encrypted. Join it, or use another folder to create a new CRM.
location.existingFirebase: This Firebase project already holds a CRM — you'll join it.
location.gitHint: Create an EMPTY private repository for the CRM data (not the repo hosting the admin).
location.gitLocalHint: A folder that is a git clone you sync yourself (Chrome / Edge).
location.gitDirHelp: Where the JSON files go (e.g. crm). Leave empty for the repository root.
location.gitHistoryBody: Every past version of every record stays in the git history, including personal data you later delete. Erasing it for good means rewriting the history (or moving to an encrypted backend).
location.gitRoles: Roles come from repository permissions: admin / maintain → admin, write → member, read → viewer.
location.firebaseHint: Everything runs in YOUR Google project; AgentCRM only needs its public web config.

firebaseSteps.project: Create a project at console.firebase.google.com (Analytics not needed).
firebaseSteps.app: Project settings → Your apps → add a Web app, copy its config below.
firebaseSteps.auth: Authentication → Sign-in method: enable Email/Password (and Google if wanted); Users → add your admin account; Settings → Authorized domains: add the domain hosting the admin.
firebaseSteps.firestore: Firestore Database → Create database (production mode, region near you).
firebaseSteps.rules: Firestore → Rules: paste the rules generated below, then Publish.

location.firebaseSnippetHelp: The fields below fill in automatically.
location.firebaseAdminHint: The account you created in Authentication → Users. Its email is pinned as bootstrap admin in the rules.

signupHelp.invite: Admins add people in Settings → Users; they join with that role on first sign-in.
signupHelp.domain: Verified addresses of these domains join as members.
signupHelp.open: Any Google / password account can join as member — your CRM data would be readable by strangers.

location.rulesHint: They are the real access control: viewers read only, members edit records and activities, admins everything. Publish them before verifying.
location.rulesNeedEmail: Enter the admin email to generate the rules.

passphrase.encryptHint: AES-256-GCM with a key derived from your passphrase (PBKDF2, 600 000 rounds). The storage provider only sees random bytes.
passphrase.label: Passphrase
passphrase.generatedCopied: Passphrase generated and copied — store it in your password manager now.
passphrase.strengthHint: At least 10 characters; a few random words work well.
passphrase.lostTitle: A lost passphrase means lost data
passphrase.lostBody: Nobody — not us, not your storage provider — can recover it. Keep it in a password manager and share it only with the people who should access the CRM.
passphrase.plainWarning: Without encryption, anyone who can read the storage (provider, leaked key, misconfigured bucket) can read your contacts.
passphrase.existingHelp: The passphrase chosen when this workspace was created.

hosting.title: Host the admin for your team (optional)
hosting.hint: Publish this admin to a static host so teammates open it at a URL. config.js (public, no secrets) is written next to it.
hosting.securityTitle: Keep the data and the admin apart
hosting.securityBody: The admin is public static files — that's fine, it holds no data and no secret. Your DATA bucket / repository must stay PRIVATE and separate from the one hosting the admin. To restrict who can even load the admin, put it behind Cloudflare Access or basic auth (docs/hosting.md).

none.title: Not now
none.description: Keep using this admin. Download config.js later to host it anywhere.

github-pages.title: GitHub Pages
github-pages.description: A repo served by GitHub Pages (free; public repo on free plans).

cloudflare-pages.title: Cloudflare Pages
cloudflare-pages.description: A Pages project connected to a repo (works with private repos).

gitlab-pages.title: GitLab Pages
gitlab-pages.description: A GitLab project with Pages (a CI file is added).

s3.title: S3 static website
s3.description: A bucket with static website hosting / a CDN in front.

local-folder.title: Local folder
local-folder.description: A folder served by a local web server or synced to a host.

zip.title: Download a ZIP
zip.description: The admin + config.js as a ZIP to upload anywhere by hand.

github-pages.title: GitHub Pages
github-pages.body: Use a repo dedicated to the admin (never the data repo). Token: fine-grained, Contents read & write (+ Pages read & write to enable Pages automatically). Leave the token empty to reuse your data token.

cloudflare-pages.title: Cloudflare Pages
cloudflare-pages.body: Connect the repo to a Pages project (no build command, output directory = the repo folder). Add Cloudflare Access to require a login before the admin loads.

gitlab-pages.title: GitLab Pages
gitlab-pages.body: The admin goes under public/ and a minimal .gitlab-ci.yml publishes it. Project access token with write_repository.

s3.title: S3 static website
s3.body: Use a DIFFERENT bucket than the data. Enable static website hosting (or a CDN like CloudFront / R2 custom domain) and allow public reads on it only.

local-folder.title: Local folder
local-folder.body: Pick the folder your web server serves; the admin is written into the sub-folder below.

hosting.folderHelp: The admin is published under this folder of the site (e.g. admin → https://…/admin/).
hosting.zipHint: The ZIP is generated at install from this (built) admin. Unzip it on any static host; config.js inside points at your data.
hosting.noneHint: You can deploy later from Settings → Admin hosting, or download config.js and copy the dist/admin files yourself.

workspace.title: Your workspace
workspace.hint: You'll be the first admin. Other people are added later in Settings → Users.
workspace.joinHint: Tell the CRM who you are on this browser.
workspace.name: Workspace name
workspace.gitEmailHelp: Used to match your git login with your CRM user (kept in this browser).
workspace.demo: Load demo data (30 companies, 80 people, 40 deals)

install.title: Ready to install
install.hint: Nothing has been written yet (except the Firebase admin record). Review and install.

summary.createDemo: Create a new CRM with demo data

steps.seed: Creating objects, pipeline and your admin user…
steps.config: Saving the configuration in this browser…

install.doneHint: This browser is configured. Teammates open the hosted admin (or your config.js) and enter their own access.
install.zipDone: The admin ZIP was downloaded — upload its content to your static host.
install.configJsBody: Put this config.js next to the admin files (dist/admin) on any static host so teammates land on this CRM. It contains no secret.

errors.publicRepo: This repository is PUBLIC: the CRM would expose personal data. Make it private first.
errors.readOnly: {{detail}} only has read access — a new CRM needs write access.
errors.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase: the data could not be decrypted.
errors.passphraseRequired: This workspace is encrypted: enter its passphrase.
errors.folderRequired: Choose (or re-grant access to) the folder first.
errors.firebaseAuth: Firebase sign-in failed (check the API key, the Email/Password provider and the credentials).
errors.firebaseUnverified: Your email address is not verified yet. We sent a verification email to {{detail}} — open the link, then verify again.
errors.firebaseWrongEmail: The signed-in account doesn't match the admin email.
errors.firebaseRules: Firestore refused the admin: publish the generated rules (with this admin email) and check Firestore is created.
errors.firebaseNotAdmin: Signed in, but the rules don't recognise you as admin (role: {{detail}}). Check the email pinned in the rules.
errors.noManifest: admin-files.json not found — deploy from a built admin (npm run build / preview), not npm run dev.

fields.endpointHelp: The S3 API URL of your provider (not the public website URL).
fields.bucketHelp: A private bucket dedicated to this CRM.
fields.forcePathStyleHelp: https://endpoint/bucket/key — needed by R2, MinIO and most S3-compatibles.
fields.publicReadHelp: For OVHcloud / Scaleway buckets that aren't public through a policy. Leave off on AWS.
fields.tokenHelp: GitHub: fine-grained token on this repo only, Contents read & write. GitLab: project access token with api / write_repository. Stays in this browser.
fields.siteUrlHelp: Where the host serves the files, e.g. https://my-company.github.io/crm-admin.

roles.adminHint: Everything: data model, pipelines, settings, users, automations, forms, hosting.
roles.memberHint: Create, edit and delete records, activities and tasks; own views; import / export.

access.folderDenied: Access to the folder was not granted.
access.storedHere: Stored in this browser only — never in config.js nor in the data.

firebase.title: Sign in to {{name}}
firebase.hint: Use the account your admin invited.
firebase.resetSent: A reset link was sent to {{email}}.
firebase.unverifiedBody: Open the verification link we emailed you, then continue.
firebase.notInvitedBody: This account has not been invited. Ask an admin to add your email in Settings → Users, then sign in again.
firebase.errorBody: Firestore refused the request. Check your connection, or ask an admin to check the security rules.

firebaseErrors.invalidEmail: This email address is not valid.
firebaseErrors.tooManyRequests: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
firebaseErrors.popupBlocked: The browser blocked the sign-in window. Allow pop-ups for this site.
firebaseErrors.unauthorizedDomain: This domain is not authorized in Firebase (Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains).
firebaseErrors.methodDisabled: This sign-in method is disabled in Firebase.

git.title: Connect to the data repository
git.hint: Enter your own access token for {{repo}}. Your repository permission decides your role.
git.githubTokenHelp: github.com → Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained tokens: this repository only, Contents read & write (read-only → viewer).
git.gitlabTokenHelp: Project → Settings → Access tokens (or a personal token) with api or write_repository scope.
git.emailHelp: Matches your git login with your CRM user (assignments, owner).
git.invalidToken: This token can't access the repository.

journal.title: Unlock this CRM on this browser
journal.hint: Data at {{location}}. Enter the access keys and passphrase your admin shared with you (once per browser).
journal.folderHint: Browsers forget folder permissions on reload: re-grant access with one click.
journal.noDataset: No AgentCRM workspace found at this location (or the keys can't read it).
journal.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase: the data could not be decrypted.

data.title: Data backend
data.stats: {{documents}} documents · {{segments}} journal files ({{pendingSegments}} not compacted) · {{tombstones}} deleted entries
data.encryptionOnHint: Files are encrypted with the workspace passphrase. Changing it re-encrypts everything; every browser then needs the new one.
data.encryptionOffHint: Files are stored unencrypted. Turn encryption on to protect personal data from anyone who can read the storage.
data.rekeyWarning: Make sure nobody else is editing: the data is compacted then re-encrypted. Other browsers and the CLI will be asked for the new passphrase.
data.rekeyDone: Data re-encrypted with the new passphrase.
data.compactHint: Physically deletes records in the trash, their activities and old automation runs.
data.compactHintJournal: Purges deleted records and rewrites the storage as one snapshot (removes history of deleted data — GDPR erasure).
data.compactConfirmBody: Deleted records and their activities are purged for good. This can't be undone.
data.exportHint: Every object, record, activity, pipeline, view and setting as one JSON file (ids preserved).
data.transferHint: Copy the whole CRM to another backend or location, ids preserved, then switch to it.
data.transferExplain: Everything is copied into the destination (which must be empty). The current data is left untouched — delete it yourself once the move is verified.
data.transferNotEmpty: The destination already holds a CRM: pick an empty location.
data.transferFirebaseUsers: Users other than you become invitations in Firebase: they join with their role on first sign-in.
data.transferDoneHint: Switch this browser to the new backend now? If the admin is hosted, its config.js is updated too.
data.configJsUpdated: config.js updated on the admin hosting.
data.configJsFailed: Could not update config.js on the hosting: {{detail}}
data.rulesHint: Re-generate and publish them in the Firebase console after changing who can join.

hosting.title: Admin hosting
hosting.devNote: Deploying copies THIS admin build (admin-files.json) — run it from a built admin (npm run build / preview), not npm run dev.

enforcement.local: Single user: this browser holds the data, no roles to enforce.
enforcement.journal: Shared storage: anyone with the storage keys and the passphrase has full access. Roles in Users are informative only.
enforcement.git-json: Enforced by the repository: your token's permission is the ceiling of your role (admin / maintain → admin, write → member, read → viewer).
enforcement.firebase: Enforced by the Firestore security rules on every request.

security.secretsHint: What this browser keeps in its local storage for this CRM:
security.neverShared: Secrets are never written to config.js, to the CRM data or to git. Other browsers enter their own.
security.forgetConfirmBody: Keys, tokens and the passphrase are removed from this browser. You'll need them again to open the CRM here.
